⚠️ Warning: 7 things your son will carry for life. And none of them are toys.

In the 1950s, Harvard asked students how caring their parents were. 35 years later, 87% of those who said their parents weren't caring had a serious illness by midlife, compared with 25% of those who felt cared for (Russek & Schwartz, Harvard Mastery of Stress Study, 1997). 🏛️

So here's what he'll carry:
1️⃣ The way you spoke. He'll forget your rules, not your tone.
2️⃣ Whether you listened. Even when he was holding a beetle. 🪲 "I matter."
3️⃣ How you handled his mistakes, when things were in pieces.
4️⃣ The little ways you showed love. A note in his lunchbox. 📝
5️⃣ Whether you compared him. At 40, he'll still ask, "Was I ever good enough?"
6️⃣ How you treated each other. That's where he learns love. 👫
7️⃣ Love without conditions. With an F on his test, does he still want to come home? 🏠

"But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him and felt compassion, and ran and embraced him and kissed him." Luke 15:20 (ESV) 🙏 That's the way the Father loves us, so that's the way we love them.

30 years later, the toys are long gone. But he still knows exactly how it felt to be your child. ❤️

BravePath Kids is a Christ-centered 21-day journey for childhood anxiety, made for parents and kids to do together:
✨ Simple anxiety skills
📖 Scripture they can hold onto
